title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. G is a group and G_0 a subgroup; C is a G-set and C_0 a subset. The standing hypothesis is that the action map G_0 × C_0 → C, (h,c) ↦ h·c, is a bijection. In other words, G_0 acts freely on C and C_0 meets every G_0-orbit exactly once, so C_0 is a global slice for the G_0-action and C/G_0 ≅ C_0.

For c ∈ C_0, Grothendieck sets G(c) = {g ∈ G | g·c ∈ C_0} and claims G(c) ≅ G_0\G. He proves this by showing that G_0 × G(c) → G, (h,g) ↦ hg, is bijective.
- Injectivity: if hg = h'g', then h'' := h'^{-1}h satisfies h''·(gc) = g'c = 1·(g'c). Both gc and g'c lie in C_0, so uniqueness in the slice gives h'' = 1, hence h = h' and g = g'.
- Surjectivity: for k ∈ G, write kc = h·c' with h ∈ G_0 and c' ∈ C_0. Then h^{-1}k ∈ G(c), so k = h·(h^{-1}k).
Thus G(c) is a system of representatives of the right cosets G_0\G (G = G_0 · G(c), uniquely). The block is struck through, apparently to be rewritten rather than because it is wrong. A marginal 'Cor' records C/G_0 ≅ C_0 and something like C/G vs G_0\G.

Under the heading 'O.S.' (orbit/stabilizer) he asks whether g·c = c with c ∈ C_0 forces g = 1, i.e. whether G acts freely. He then takes a G-orbit O and wants O ∩ C_0 ≅ G_0\G, writing x = h·c_0 uniquely before breaking off.
- In general O ∩ C_0 ≅ G_0\O ≅ G_0\G/Stab(c), since O ≅ G/Stab(c) and G_0 acts freely on O.
- So the claimed identification needs Stab(c) = 1, which is exactly the question he flags.

Purpose in the manuscript. The previous page computes how a 'connection' C on the completed symmetric algebra of Ω transforms under formal coordinate changes ω ↦ ω^u = ω(1+Σ_{i≥2} α_i ω^i). It also imposes the normal form C(ω_0) = ϖ_0 + ω_0ϖ_1 + ω_0^2ϖ_2. The next page sets up algebra connections on the complete augmented algebra P ≅ Sym^(Ω).
- The plausible reading is that G is the group of formal coordinate changes (Aut of the formal disc, or of jets), G_0 a subgroup such as the tangent-to-identity part, C the set of formal connections, and C_0 a normal-form slice (e.g. 'quadratic' connections).
- The lemma then counts how many normal forms lie in one G-orbit. Those normal forms correspond to reductions of the coordinate-change group to a smaller group, plausibly PGL_2 or its Borel; this is how projective connections arise as residual structure.
errors: In the struck-out injectivity argument the hypothesis is written 'g, g' ∈ G_0'; it should be g, g' ∈ G(c).
'G(c) ≅ G/G_0' should be the right-coset space G_0\G, since the decomposition proved is G = G_0·G(c).
The final claim O ∩ C_0 ≅ G_0\G holds only if the stabilizer of c in G is trivial. In general it is G_0\G/Stab_G(c). Grothendieck himself flags this ('gc = c ⇒ g = 1 ?') and leaves it unresolved.

ideas.what: If a subgroup G_0 acts on a G-set C with a global slice C_0, then for c ∈ C_0 the set of g with gc ∈ C_0 is a transversal for G_0\G, and orbit ∩ slice ≅ G_0\G/Stab
ideas.modern_name: slice / transversal lemma, orbit-stabilizer; reduction of structure group via normal forms

ideas.what: Using this lemma to compare normal forms of formal connections (under the group of formal coordinate changes) with a coset space of that group, in the context of projective connections
ideas.modern_name: projective structures as reduction of the Aut(O)-torsor of formal coordinates to PGL_2 (opers / Schwarzian normal form)

deep.surprise_reason: An elementary group-action lemma (slice/transversal plus orbit-stabilizer), serving as a bookkeeping step for normal forms of formal connections. It is correct up to a freeness hypothesis that Grothendieck himself flags, and nothing on the page is new.
transcription_corrections: In the injectivity block the hypothesis reads 'g, g' ∈ G(c)' in intent; the transcription's 'g, g' ∈ G_0' is either a slip of the pen or a misreading.
The first map reads (h,c) ↦ h.c; the 'h' was first written as something like 'g' and overwritten.
'Soit c ∈ C_0, et soit G(c) = {g ∈ G | g.c ∈ C_0}' is correctly read.
The marginal note reads roughly 'Cor C/G_0 ≃ C_0 ens. quotient (bij...) ; Revoir C/G_0 ... C/G ≃ G_0\G' (uncertain).
Near the bottom, 'Ad\G' appears overwritten to read G_0\G; the final line 'x = h.c_0 (h ∈ G_0, c_0 ∈ C_0, uniques)' is followed by a struck 'donc OPS x ∈ C_0 ... g.h.c'.
